history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 159 (Someshwar Nath Mahadev Temple, Areraj — same temple, filed under a different CSV row). The Someshwar Nath Mahadev Temple at Areraj, East Champaran district (CSV town 'Motihari' corrected to Areraj; Areraj is ~28-30 km south-west of Motihari), is one of North Bihar's most-visited Shiva shrines, near the Nepal border. Per the Bihar tourism department and Shiv Puran tradition, King Som built the 55-ft-high temple about 2,000 years ago; its five-faced (Panchmukhi) lingam of Mahadeo is believed self-existent (swayambhu). Lakhs of pilgrims come from across Bihar and Nepal for the Shrawani Mela (July-August), when Kanwariyas bring Ganga jal from Sultanganj, and for Mahashivratri. The Shri Someshwar Nath Mahadev Mandir Nyas Samiti-Areraj trust was set up on 21 Aug 2006. Areraj Kund (sacred tank) is at the site, and the Lauriya Areraj Ashokan pillar (249 BCE) stands nearby.

name: Someshwar Nath Mahadev Temple, Areraj
town_description: Areraj is a small town in East Champaran district of northern Bihar, about 28-30 km south-west of the district headquarters Motihari, near the Nepal border. It is known as the Someshwar Nath Dham, a major Shiva pilgrimage centre, and for the nearby Lauriya Areraj Ashokan pillar (249 BCE). The town sits on the banks of the Teli (Telie) river.

travel.road: Pucca road from Motihari, ~28 km south-west to Areraj
